content: Hereditary sensory neuropathy type II (HSN2) is a protein in humans encoded by the HSN2 gene. This protein is derived from a single-exon open reading frame (ORF) and represents a nervous system-specific exon of the WNK1 gene. HSN2 is an alternatively spliced exon of WNK1, and this splicing event occurs selectively in nervous tissues, leading to the formation of WNK1/HSN2 isoforms specific to the nervous system. The WNK1/HSN2 isoforms are expressed in sensory regions of both the peripheral and central nervous systems, which are involved in the transmission of sensory and nociceptive signals. These regions include satellite cells, Schwann cells, and sensory neurons. The novel protein product of this isoform is more abundant in sensory neurons compared to motor neurons. It is hypothesized that this gene product may play a role in the development and/or maintenance of peripheral sensory neurons or their supporting Schwann cells. Mutations in the HSN2 gene are associated with congenital sensory neuropathy (HSAN Type II), an autosomal recessive disorder. This condition is characterized by impaired pain, temperature, and touch sensation due to a reduction or absence of peripheral sensory neurons.
